# Affine — subnet 120

Public dashboard: https://affine.io/
Public measurement data: https://affine.io/network-data.json
Source and documentation: https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine

Affine is an experimental synchronous inference-verification training subnet.
The current rewrite pilot is nonpayable and does not submit blockchain weights.
Historical teacher distillation / king-versus-challenger instructions are not the
current pilot contract. Dashboard records describe measured runs, not a promise
of rewards, general model improvement, or support for every environment.

Current operational status: the first v11 revision2 public math epoch is fully
qualified and closed for uploads. Its signed deadline was 2026-10-03 08:09:37 UTC.
Admission is open to every activated subnet-120 hotkey, with no operator whitelist.
Six miners passed full independent verification, including UID 85, and received
proposed nonpayable shares of 1/6 each. One actual full-model update consumed one
accepted pair; the other five pairs were not used in that update. Its successor
checkpoint is published, with four cumulative updates. Matched fixed32 evaluation
changed from 23/32 to 22/32. The controller exited cleanly without operator
recovery. This small cohort does not establish broader improvement.
The latest published epoch uses that successor, with 237 activated identities
including UID 85 and all 6,746 original MATH tasks. Its signed deadline is
2026-10-03 09:54:20 UTC. Read https://affine.io/mining.json for the signed current
manifest, source pin and current open/closed status before submitting. Its upload
window has now closed. All five submitted batches passed independent full audits,
earning one unique point each and proposed nonpayable shares of 0.2. The baseline
repeated at 22/32; one full-model update produced a new checkpoint. All ten
checkpoint files passed content hashes, and the separate after evaluation

closeout passed with an actual clean controller exit and no operator recovery.
Two consecutive public epochs are now qualified, with five cumulative updates.
The separate original I3Math generation test finished with a genuine success/
failure pair and native self-verification. It has not completed independent
public-epoch verification or training. The next MATH opening is being prepared
with the new sampled audit source and a prospective live reward contract.
Blockchain weight submission remains disabled.

## Architecture

The validator/controller opens an epoch with an immutable signed manifest. It
pins the checkpoint file hashes, approved source bundle, environment/task pool,
harness, numerical/runtime profile, K/L requirements, upload bounds and deadline.
The miner downloads and checks those exact bytes and samples the target model.
A batch concerns one authorized task index and contains positive and negative
rollouts, complete context/output tokens, full conditional model probabilities,
TOPLOC activation fingerprints and native environment observations/outcomes.
The current pilot requires K=1 positive and L=1 negative rollout for that task.
An unsuccessful search is not a completed batch. Held-out tasks may not be mined.

Miners upload one cumulative private artifact through a sealed, per-identity R2
capability. Only a final upload completed before the signed deadline is eligible.
At the deadline, the controller freezes immutable, hash-addressed bytes and audit
receipts. It does not change the deadline to rescue a failed worker. Later uploads
cannot replace a frozen submission. Private capabilities and credentials are not
public API links and must not be shared.

Separate verifier workers recompute the target-model distributions and TOPLOC
fingerprints under the approved runtime, and replay the original environment
and native grader. Uploaded content cannot select executable code or grading.
Numerical/hardware compatibility must be qualified for the signed profile;
a proof from one runtime is not automatically portable to another.

Invalid batches score zero. A valid unique task key
(checkpoint, environment ID, sample index) earns one test point. When multiple
miners submit valid batches for that same key, everyone scores zero for that key.
Duplicate valid batches can remain eligible training data; scoring uniqueness
and training eligibility are distinct. The current pilot performs full audits.
Optional research sampling does not make unchecked batches eligible for training
and leaves duplicate coverage / scores provisional.

The trainer receives only verified positive/negative pairs and performs a
reference-relative sequence-preference gradient update against the immutable
reference checkpoint. The objective is experimental. Verified replay requires
approved provenance and exact attribution. The successor checkpoint is hashed
file by file before the next synchronous epoch can use it. An empty epoch has
no fabricated batch, optimizer update or miner reward. Failed/aborted runs remain
preserved rather than being rewritten as successful epochs.

Roles are logically separate: miner searches; verifier checks inference and
native outcomes; trainer updates weights; validator/controller owns admission,
deadlines, freeze, scoring and checkpoint handover. The new separated pilot uses
five distinct H200 hosts: one miner, two verifiers, one trainer and one evaluator.
Arbos.life is the local operator/validator host. This physical separation does
not by itself establish production decentralization.

## What the two charts measure

Evaluation performance is the actual mean native reward over completed held-out
samples at the recorded completion time. Comparable cohorts bind model family,
environment version, dataset/taskset hashes, fixed task IDs, seed, sample count,
harness, output budget, policy and runtime. Checkpoint weights can change within
one cohort. Repeated evaluations of the same checkpoint remain visible as
separate measurements. Distinct cohorts are never joined into a single curve.
Curated candidate controls are labelled; they do not prove autonomous solving.
Explicit recovery records remain distinct from incomplete original attempts.

Batches per epoch counts frozen submitted batches in finalized scoring windows,
including rejected and unchecked batches. Tooltips distinguish accepted,
rejected and unchecked counts. Finalized scoring does not by itself establish
completed training. The series selector separates the original MATH pilot from
historical experiments; Network and Pilot tests remain separate scopes.
There are no invented live metrics or projected evaluations.

The original MATH pilot starts with the untouched SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct base and
7,496 distinct original tasks: 6,746 mining tasks and 750 reserved evaluation
tasks. Its initial fixed held-out cohort has 32 tasks and a 256-token output
budget. The first three completed training epochs made 24 actual optimizer
updates. Distinct base/successor checkpoints scored 6, 7, 9 and 9 correct out of
32. This small fixed cohort does not establish broad mathematical improvement.
The historical affine_numina environment uses Lean tasks; it is not the new
NuminaMath-CoT corpus. Preparing or qualifying a new corpus is not evaluation
or completed training evidence. New measurement cohorts appear only when actual
completed records have been published.

The separate H200 pilot uses Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct, 1,024-token outputs and
a different fixed cohort of 32 reserved Level 4/5 tasks. Its first full-model
training update changed actual parameter values and its checkpoint was recovered
and independently verified in R2. The original baseline and successor evaluation
remain errors because one generated sample failed the old TOPLOC replay path.
The encoded index-map correction passed on an independent H200 verifier with
zero-error thresholds unchanged; the honest sample passed and four tampered
controls failed. Fresh corrected-source evaluations completed all 32 tasks:
the untouched base and trained successor both solved 20/32 (mean reward 0.625).
Two tasks improved and two declined, so the measured aggregate gain is zero.
This is a small fixed cohort, not an accuracy estimate for all 7,496 problems.
These Qwen measurements must not be joined to the older SmolLM2 curve.

## How to try the pilot

Open admission policy admits every current subnet
120 identity with a valid signed Ed25519 Affine activation, without individual
operator approval. Each epoch takes a fresh chain snapshot; later activations
enter the next epoch. The signed authority, discovery URL and pinned runtime
remain required. The last published signed epoch included 237 eligible identities,
including UID 85. No blockchain action
is required merely to read the public dashboard.

Start with the public repository and these guides:
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/MINER_QUICKSTART.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/MATH_MINER_BOOTSTRAP.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/MATH_PILOT.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
- https://github.com/AffineFoundation/affine/blob/main/docs/DISTRIBUTED_GPU_ROLES.md

A clean checkout needs the generated task snapshot and exact signed source.
Use the source bootstrap with the published authority and fresh discovery URL:

CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 python -B -m subnet.source_bootstrap \
  --authority "$AFFINE_OPERATOR_AUTHORITY" \
  --current-url "$AFFINE_SIGNED_CURRENT_URL" \
  --source-cache /absolute/private/source-cache \
  --key /absolute/private/miner.key \
  --state /absolute/private/miner-state --once

Get the authority and read-only current_url from https://affine.io/mining.json.
Set AFFINE_OPERATOR_AUTHORITY and AFFINE_SIGNED_CURRENT_URL to those values.
This metadata grants no bucket write access; uploads remain encrypted per miner.
Use your own miner Ed25519 key in a private file; never disclose a mnemonic,
coldkey, wallet file, bucket credential or decrypted signed upload capability.
The bootstrap checks signed manifests, source/archive hashes and membership
before running the admitted CLI in a fresh isolated interpreter. Runtime packages
still need installing and qualifying on your hardware. Source changes require
fresh bootstrap approval; source is signed executable code, not a sandbox.

The historical SmolLM2 baseline uses CUDA compute capability 8.6. The new H200
Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct pilot pins model revision
ef9926d75ab1d54532f6a30dd5e760355eb9aa4d and CUDA compute capability 9.0,
BF16, eager attention and deterministic CUBLAS. Genuine same-model generation,
full-vocabulary probability and TOPLOC proof controls passed on the miner and
both independent verifiers, including rejection of altered evidence. Those
controls are hardware qualification, not held-out evaluations or training.
The first real separated epoch completed one full-model training update and
checkpoint publication. The corrected-source public-client epoch
nonpayable-separated-hopper-original-math-v8-1790992415-0 opened on October 3,
with a signed deadline of 02:23:35 UTC. Its manifest was independently checked
against the approved checkpoint and full mining pool. Two independent verifier
workers are running. The owned miner's first bootstrap exited before downloading
source or model bytes: it requires a `url` source descriptor field, while the
manifest supplies `read_url`. The attempt and original deadline are preserved;
a corrected descriptor is being qualified for a fresh epoch. No upload, audit
or training from this public-client attempt is claimed.
The original window closed with zero submitted batches and zero points. Its
fixed held-out evaluations completed all 32 tasks before and after, scoring
20/32 in both with unchanged weights. No mining or optimizer update occurred. The
descriptor correction passed a separate diagnostic bootstrap on the actual
Lium miner, including signed R2 source download and exact file admission; that
diagnostic stopped before the CLI or model and is not a mining result.
An earlier activation attempt stopped because the retained miner's SSH endpoint
refused connections; its single reboot failed with "Executor unreachable".
The replacement H200 passed source, model, runtime and proof qualification before
activation. The failed pod and original records are retained.
Neither these controls nor the fresh paired
evaluation establish a performance gain. Exact installed versions and source policies come
from the signed challenge. Other hardware compatibility is unproven.
Report only public epoch IDs/hotkeys, hardware/runtime and errors with secrets
and signed URLs removed. Pilot points are permanently nonpayable. The separate
legacy transition writer is outside this pilot; charts are not chain payouts.

The v9 epoch nonpayable-separated-hopper-original-math-v9-1790996840-0
opened at 03:07:20 UTC on October 3, 2026 and closed at 03:37:20 UTC.
Its signed R2 manifest includes all 239 authenticated activation identities,
all 6,746 mining tasks and the fixed 32 held-out tasks. Operator allowlisting
is disabled. Later activations are discovered at the next epoch opening.
Root verified the published manifest and public discovery HTTPS readback.
UIDs 131 and 168 each submitted a genuine positive/negative batch, independently
verified on two H200 verifier nodes. Each earned one nonpayable test point and
proposed weight 0.5. One full-model AdamW update used UID 168's pair; UID 131's
pair was accepted but unused in this one-step update. All ten successor files
were independently verified in R2. The matched fixed32 evaluation changed from
20/32 to 22/32. This two-task gain is a cohort measurement, not an established
broader trend.

Final history publication then failed because the history reader expected a
source bucket key absent from the signed bootstrap descriptor. A follow-on
opening hit the same error. The old manifests, deadlines, checkpoint, training
counter and failed attempts are retained. The separately signed repaired v10
release admitted the published v9 successor checkpoint and retained cumulative
training step 2 and round 1. Root independently verified repaired history and the
fresh signed R2 opening, with 239 eligible activation identities including UID 85
and all 6,746 mining tasks. The old signed source is not hotpatched and training
is not repeated. V10 is an actual opening, not a completed new training epoch or
new gain measurement. Full consecutive-epoch qualification remains pending;
chain weight submission stays disabled.

## Agent-operated mining and version updates

Use an agent to manage your miner, monitor signed epoch discovery and this guide,
and report operational failures with credentials removed. Watch GitHub main
continually for upgrades. The signed epoch source SHA remains authoritative:
never hot-reload arbitrary main code into an active epoch. At a source change,
rerun the signed-source bootstrap in a fresh admitted cache before mining the
new challenge. Checkpoint changes within the approved source use the normal
immutable checkpoint download/hash checks.

The prepared bounded policy limits batches per UID and total expensive audits,
uses a post-freeze random selection, and reserves additional work after confirmed
invalid samples. Only fully verified unique observed tasks earn proposed points;
unchecked batches never enter training or earn points. Unknown infrastructure
failures retry without fraud penalties. The prepared default multiplies a miner's
epoch points by 0.5 per confirmed invalid batch, with whole-epoch zeroing disabled.
The signed opening manifest defines the actual limits and parameters; defaults
are not retroactive rules for historical full-audit epochs. Sampled scoring does
not prove global uniqueness among unchecked submissions.

Prospective live rewards will use a separate signed reward contract and one
local chain writer. Compute nodes remain unable to sign chain transactions.
Old nonpayable pilot epochs will not become payable. As of this launch-preparation
notice, the new writer has not submitted weights and the live reward opening
has not been published.
